title: [08/02/2025] UK visitors to Spain by age group
prompt: The graphs below show the age of visitors from the UK to Spain in 1983 and 2003. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts compare the age distribution of UK visitors to Spain in 1983 and 2003.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, visitor numbers generally grew for those aged 0-15, 16-24, and over 55. Meanwhile, the percentage of visitors from the 34-54 age group remained the largest despite experiencing the most significant decline.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding increasing groups, in 1983, visitors aged 55 and above represented 16%, those aged 0-15 accounted for 10%, and the age 16-24 bracket made up 4%. By 2003, the figure for the oldest age category had increased substantially to 26%, becoming the second-largest segment. Similarly, the proportion of the 16-24-year-old group rose dramatically to 15%, nearly quadrupling from its initial level, while that of the youngest category increased modestly to 12%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the declining categories, in 1983, the 34-54 demographic dominated with exactly half of all UK visitors to Spain, while visitors aged 25-34 represented 20% of the total. However, both experienced considerable decreases by 2003, with the proportion of the 34-54 segment falling to 35% and the percentage for the 25-34 category dropping to 12%. Despite recording the most substantial decline of 15 percent, the 34-54 group maintained its position as the largest segment.
